unresolved.notes:
File7 can't be repaired from venues.json: its site is now a JavaScript ticketing app, and the dates are only in each event page's JSON-LD, which the "llm" strategy throws away. It needs a new parser, written by a human.

Cause: www.file7.com (including /agenda) now serves the "La Billetterie" / Sonic web-component app of billetterie.file7.com. The pages are empty shells (<sonic-home>, <sonic-tickets-app>) that JavaScript fills from /api/v2, and that API answers HTTP 401 without a token (/api/v2/events, /api/v2/sessions).
What I tried: www.file7.com/, /agenda, robots.txt, billetterie.file7.com/agenda and rss.xml (empty Drupal feed) all give 0 characters of usable text. https://billetterie.file7.com/sitemap.xml lists about 19 event pages (/agenda/<id>-<SLUG>), but it has no dates. Pointing the LLM at it would only make it guess dates, so I did not use it.
Where the data is: each event page (e.g. https://billetterie.file7.com/agenda/439-INTO-THE-WOODS) has a schema.org Event JSON-LD block in <head>, with name, startDate, prices, availability and url. html_to_text drops <head> and <script>, so the LLM strategy sees nothing.
Suggestion for a human: write a parser in venues_html.py, for example "file7". It would get() the sitemap, collect the /agenda/<id>-... URLs, get() each one, and json.loads its application/ld+json Event (name, startDate, offers price/availability, url). That's about 20 requests per run, and the same parser would probably work for other "La Billetterie" sites. Then register it in STRATEGIES (sources/__init__.py), which is outside what I'm allowed to change here.
What I changed: nothing (venues.json and the parsers are untouched).
Check result: ok=false, count 0 (prev 9), "the page holds 33 characters of text (JavaScript-rendered page or bot wall?)".
None of the pages I fetched contained instructions aimed at an agent.

Duc des Lombards replaced its site with a JavaScript-only "La Billetterie" ticketing app whose event API needs a bearer token, so it cannot be repaired from venues.json; nothing was changed.

Cause: https://www.ducdeslombards.com/ (and ducdeslombards.com, /feed/, /sitemap.xml) now serve the same 38 KB HTML shell of
the billetterie.ducdeslombards.com app (<sonic-tickets-app>, <sonic-home>), with no concert text in it. The events are loaded in the browser.
- https://billetterie.ducdeslombards.com/agenda: same empty shell (title "Agenda | Duc des Lombards", 0 characters of text).
- https://billetterie.ducdeslombards.com/api/v2/events: HTTP 401. The app sends an "Authorization: Bearer <token>" header,
  using a public token embedded in the page. livemusic.fetch.get cannot send custom headers, so no "url"/"urls" change can reach it.
- I found no RSS, WordPress or static agenda page.
No page contained instructions aimed at the scraper.

Changed: nothing. The check still fails with the same error (0 events, page with no text).

For a human: write a dedicated parser/strategy for the La Billetterie API (GET https://billetterie.ducdeslombards.com/api/v2/...
with the Bearer token from the page's <sonic-tickets-app token="...">). That needs header support in livemusic.fetch.
Or find out whether the venue publishes its programme elsewhere (newsletter, a partner listing).

Not repairable from here: fgo-barbara.fr answers HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) to every URL on the domain, so the site is rate-limiting or blocking the scraper as a whole.

Cause: since 2026-10-24 the scraper's requests to the site are refused with 429. I tested:
- https://fgo-barbara.fr/programmation (the configured URL)
- https://fgo-barbara.fr/ (home page)
- https://fgo-barbara.fr/feed/ (RSS)
- https://fgo-barbara.fr/wp-json/wp/v2/pages (WordPress REST)
- https://www.fgo-barbara.fr/programmation
All returned 429. No page loaded, so no other URL can be used in venues.json.

What I changed: nothing. venues.json and the parsers are as they were.

Check result: {"ok": false, "count": 0, "prev_count": 28, "error": "HTTP 429 for https://fgo-barbara.fr/programmation"}

What a human should do: open the site in a normal browser from another network to see whether this is an IP or user-agent block (bot wall / WAF) or a temporary rate limit. If the block lasts, ask the venue for access or a feed, or find the programme somewhere else, such as a ticketing site or the Ville de Paris agenda. That would need a new URL and possibly a new parser. If the 429 goes away on its own, the source should work again with no change.

Not repairable from here: lestroisbaudets.com answers HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) to every URL the scraper fetches, so the whole site is blocking or rate-limiting it, not just the agenda page.
Cause: the whole domain returns 429 to the scraper's fetcher: /l-agenda, the homepage /, /wp-json/ and /feed/ all fail the same way. It has done so on every run since 2026-10-24 (3 days), so it looks like a lasting block (WAF/anti-bot or IP rate limit), not a one-off spike.
Changed: nothing. No other URL on the site can be fetched, and the fix isn't in venues.json or a parser.
Check result: ok=false, count=0, error "HTTP 429 for https://lestroisbaudets.com/l-agenda" (previous count 30).
For a human: open the agenda in a normal browser from the scraper's network to see whether the IP or user agent is blocked. If it is, contact the venue or lower the request rate. Also look for another source for the programme (a ticketing partner page, an export or feed). If the block stays, think about a different fetch method (outside what this agent may change).
No instructions were found in page content (no page content could be downloaded).
